text:
Calgary and Seattle have already seen plenty of each other this fall, and the earlier meetings were blowouts. Less than a week after the Flames won 6-2, this one was the opposite: a 2-1 game decided 55 seconds into overtime, when Matty Beniers took a Brandon Montour pass and beat Dustin Wolf with a wrist shot.

Calgary scored first. Yegor Sharangovich tipped one in at 12:45 of the first, with Zach Whitecloud and Morgan Frost assisting, and that assist was a milestone for Frost: his 200th career point. Wolf kept it 1-0 by stopping Bobby McMann on a 28% look in the first, Seattle's best chance of the night that didn't go in.

The tying goal came from nothing. Berkly Catton, the 8th overall pick in 2024 who put up 109 points in his last WHL season, scored at 13:09 of the second on a wrist shot with a 5% chance of going in, the least likely goal of the game. Mackie Samoskevich and Kaapo Kakko assisted. It moved Seattle from a 31% chance of winning to 52%, and the third period passed without either side finding another.

By the numbers this was as even as hockey gets. Expected goals, the quality of each side's chances, finished 2.77 to 2.47 for Seattle; Calgary had more shot attempts, 64 to 56. Replay every shot and the Kraken win 55% of the time. Both goalies were better than their workload. Joey Daccord stopped 25 of 26 and saved 1.5 goals more than expected, good enough for the third star, and Wolf saved 0.77 more than expected on 29 shots.

Beniers had only one shot on goal all night, and it was the one that counted. That's the cruel arithmetic of overtime: Seattle's win chance went from 52% to 100% on a 25% look. For Calgary, a goal from Sharangovich and a milestone for Frost is the consolation, and a goaltender who keeps giving them a chance in games like this one is the bigger one.
headline: Beniers ends a tight one in overtime
